items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: The first set of Nestico/Basie charts had just come out

ctx.x: How were you hired here? What credentials did you have? Because there was no jazz program to graduate from at the time, was there?

Well it would probably be interesting to just take a few minutes to give a little bit of the background and the scene at Kent State at that time. When I started the program there, the jazz education programs that existed like at North Texas State and Berklee for example, those were really the exceptions. And most music schools in the early 1960s, jazz was a forbidden kind of thing. So at Kent State nobody wanted to have jazz and we had our problems with being kicked out of practice rooms and nobody wants to do…

back he said, “Well you have to invite me back next year, and next year I’ll come back and bring Joe Williams with me.” And we said, “Clark, I don’t know if we can afford that, our budget is really small.” He said, “Don’t worry, I’ll come for half as much.”
